mainTopic: בל תאחר: the daily violation, how the year and the רגלים are counted, and who is subject to it (heir, woman, בכור)
overview: This amud opens at the end of רב זביד's answer to an earlier difficulty: the offspring was eaten 'on the חג' (סוכות) because it was sick on שבועות. רב אשי answers instead that 'חג' there means שבועות. The גמרא explains that רב זביד rejects this because a תנא who mentions פסח calls שבועות 'עצרת'. Next, רבא rules that once three רגלים have passed, a person transgresses בל תאחר every single day. A ברייתא is brought against him, and רבא answers that the תנא only wanted to set the point where the first violation begins. The גמרא then asks how a year can pass without three רגלים. It answers for רבי with a leap year, and for the רבנן with רב שמעיה's teaching that שבועות can fall on the 5th, 6th or 7th of סיון, which אחרים dispute. רבי זירא then asks whether an heir and whether a woman are subject to בל תאחר. The heir is excluded by the word מֵעִמָּךְ. For the woman, אביי ties the answer to her obligation in שמחה, speaking according to רבי זירא's view. Finally, אביי and רב אחא בר יעקב discuss when a בכור's year begins, and the גמרא starts to show they do not truly disagree. That reconciliation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The offspring was sick on שבועות
steps.stepSummary: The end of רב זביד's answer: the offspring was not brought on שבועות because it was sick then, so it was brought on סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: [It is a case] where it was sick on עצרת (שבועות).
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of רב זביד's answer to an earlier difficulty. He explains that the offspring was eaten on סוכות only because it was sick on שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בריתא said the offspring was eaten as שלמים 'on the חג', which normally means סוכות. That seemed strange, because it should have been offered earlier, on שבועות. רב זביד answers that the animal was sick on שבועות, so it could not go on the מזבח until the next festival.

keyTerms.meaning: sick (an animal unfit to be offered at that time)
the term the משנה and בריתא use for שבועות

phrases.english: where it was sick on Atzeret (Shavuot).
phrases.notes: This finishes רב זביד's answer from the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב זביד's answer, which began on the previous amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The offspring was needlessly delayed until סוכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was delayed only because it was sick and unfit on שבועות.

steps.title: רב אשי: 'the חג' here means שבועות
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers another answer: the word 'חג' in this בריתא refers to שבועות, not סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What does the phrase 'and we ate its offspring as שלמים on the חג' that the בריתא teaches mean? The festival of שבועות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer to the same difficulty. He says the 'חג' mentioned in the בריתא is שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of adding a special detail like sickness, רב אשי rereads one word. If 'חג' means שבועות, then the offspring was offered on time and the difficulty disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: its offspring (of the consecrated animal)
peace-offerings
'the festival', usually סוכות
the festival of שבועות

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
What is the 'and we ate its offspring as peace-offerings on the Festival' that it teaches?
The festival of Shavuot.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מַאי ״וְאָכַלְנוּ וְלָדָהּ שְׁלָמִים בֶּחָג״ דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same difficulty that רב זביד answered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'חג' means סוכות, so the offspring was offered late.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חג' here means שבועות, so there was no delay.

steps.title: Why didn't the other אמורא say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב זביד did not accept רב אשי's simpler reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רב זביד)?
steps.whatsHappening: This one word is the גמרא's question: why did רב זביד not explain it the way רב אשי did? It sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's answer seems easier, because it needs no special case like sickness. So the גמרא wants to know what pushed רב זביד away from it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and the other one?' (why didn't the other אמורא say this?)

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: A quick question; the answer comes right after.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why רב זביד rejected רב אשי's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רב זביד's reason for not explaining 'חג' as שבועות?

steps.title: Where פסח is named, שבועות is called עצרת
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד's reason: whenever the תנא mentions פסח, he calls שבועות 'עצרת', so 'חג' must mean סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wherever the תנא teaches 'פסח', he teaches 'עצרת' [for שבועות, not 'חג'].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב זביד follows a consistent style rule of the תנאים. When פסח is named, שבועות is called עצרת, so 'חג' can only mean סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is an argument about language. The same בריתא spoke about פסח, so had it meant שבועות it would have said 'עצרת'. That is why רב זביד needed the sickness case instead.

keyTerms.meaning: wherever, in every place that
that he (the תנא) teaches
Passover

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'חג' can never mean שבועות. רב זביד's point is about this context: when פסח is mentioned alongside, the תנא's style calls שבועות 'עצרת'.

phrases.english: Anywhere that he teaches 'Pesach',
he teaches 'Atzeret'.
phrases.notes: So 'חג' in such a context means סוכות.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּתָנֵי פֶּסַח, תָּנֵי עֲצֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 and explains why רב זביד rejects רב אשי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא's style uses 'עצרת' for שבועות whenever פסח is mentioned, so 'חג' must be סוכות.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the 'eaten on the חג' difficulty: רב זביד says the animal was sick on שבועות; רב אשי says 'חג' means שבועות. רב זביד rejects רב אשי because the תנא calls שבועות 'עצרת'.

steps.title: רבא: after three festivals, one transgresses every day
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that once three רגלים have passed, the owner transgresses בל תאחר again every single day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Once three festivals have passed over him, every single day he transgresses 'בל תאחר' (do not delay).
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. רבא says that after three רגלים pass without bringing the קרבן, the owner violates בל תאחר anew each day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether בל תאחר is a single violation at the moment the deadline passes, or a continuing one. רבא says it keeps renewing daily.

keyTerms.meaning: the three pilgrimage festivals
every single day
the prohibition 'you shall not delay' paying a vow or offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines the nature of the איסור: a continuing daily violation rather than a single one.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Once three Festivals have passed over him,

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם וָיוֹם עוֹבֵר בְּ״בַל תְּאַחֵר״.
phrases.english: every single day he transgresses 'You shall not delay'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָבְרוּ עָלָיו שְׁלֹשָׁה רְגָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the timing of the בל תאחר violation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After three רגלים, בל תאחר is transgressed again every day.

steps.title: ברייתא: a year without festivals, or festivals without a year
steps.stepSummary: A בריתא is brought: for a בכור and all קדשים, a year without three רגלים, or three רגלים without a year, is enough for בל תאחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: Both a firstborn and all consecrated animals, once a year has passed over them without [three] festivals, or [three] festivals without a year, he transgresses 'בל תאחר'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a בריתא to challenge רבא, using the formal word מיתיבי. At this point it is not yet clear why it contradicts him; the next steps explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בריתא widens when בל תאחר applies: a full year can trigger it even without three festivals, and three festivals can trigger it even before a year passes. It says nothing about a daily violation.

keyTerms.meaning: a firstborn animal, given to the כהן
consecrated offerings
a year passing without the three festivals

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Both a firstborn and all consecrated animals,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָבְרוּ עֲלֵיהֶם שָׁנָה בְּלֹא רְגָלִים,
phrases.english: once a year has passed over them without Festivals,
or Festivals without a year —
he transgresses 'You shall not delay'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אֶחָד בְּכוֹר, וְאֶחָד כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from a בריתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that one transgresses every day after three רגלים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בריתא lists the ways to violate בל תאחר but leaves out a daily violation (spelled out in step 8).

steps.title: What is the objection here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: the בריתא does not seem to say anything against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the refutation from this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the objection itself. The בריתא does not directly argue with רבא, so where is the contradiction? This sets up רב כהנא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בריתא talks about when the violation starts, and רבא talks about what happens afterward. On the surface they do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: his refutation (the strong objection against him)

phrases.english: And what is the refutation from this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the objection of step 6 is relevant to רבא at all.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does the בריתא contradict רבא?

steps.title: רב כהנא: the תנא is listing prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that the objection is valid: the תנא is collecting cases of לאווין, so he should have added the daily violation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The one who objects objects well. Since the תנא is searching for לאווין, let him teach: 'every single day he transgresses בל תאחר.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא defends the objection and explains it. The בריתא is going out of its way to list extra violations, so its silence about a daily violation suggests there is none.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a proof from silence. A תנא who is adding more cases of the לאו would surely mention the most extreme one, a new violation every day. Since he does not, it looks like רבא is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: he objects well (the objection is valid)
since, after all
he is searching for prohibitions
let him teach (he should have taught)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא argues from what a list leaves out: when a source is clearly collecting cases, a missing case is significant.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּקָא מוֹתֵיב — שַׁפִּיר קָא מוֹתֵיב:
phrases.english: He who objects — objects well:
Since the Tanna is seeking out prohibitions,

phrases.aramaic: לִיתְנֵי: בְּכׇל יוֹם וָיוֹם עוֹבֵר בְּ״בַל תְּאַחֵר״.
phrases.english: let him teach: every single day he transgresses 'You shall not delay'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: מַאן דְּקָא מוֹתֵיב שַׁפִּיר קָא מוֹתֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by explaining the objection, which renews the challenge to רבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בריתא is listing לאווין, so leaving out the daily violation implies it does not exist, against רבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Proof from silence: a תנא collecting violations would have mentioned the daily one.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא says בל תאחר renews daily after three רגלים. The בריתא, as רב כהנא explains it, challenges him because a תנא listing violations should have mentioned that.

steps.title: רבא's defense: the תנא only needed to set up one prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the challenge. The תנא of the בריתא only wanted to show when the person first becomes guilty of a לאו. He was not trying to list every extra לאו after that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other (רבא), how does he explain it? The תנא was looking to establish the case as a לאו. He was not looking to add extra לאווין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבא's answer to the challenge from the בריתא. רבא says the בריתא simply did not need to mention the daily violation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא argued that the בריתא should have mentioned the daily violation, since it was listing לאווין. רבא's side answers that the בריתא only wanted to set the starting point, the moment you first break בל תאחר. Once that point is set, the תנא had no need to list extra violations, so his silence does not disprove רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: how does the other opinion (here רבא) explain it?
To establish it, to fix it
He is searching for, trying to get
Extra prohibitions

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's ruling (a new violation every day after three רגלים) stays in place. The בריתא only defines when the first violation begins.

phrases.english: And the other (Rava), how does he explain it?
The tanna is looking to establish it with a prohibition;
he is not looking for extra prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's claim (Step 8) that the בריתא contradicts רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the purpose of the source (the תנא's goal was limited)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the תנא was listing לאווין, his silence about a daily violation shows there is none.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא only aimed to set the first point of violation, so his silence proves nothing against רבא.

steps.title: Returning to the ברייתא: how can a year pass without three Festivals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the בריתא itself. It accepts that three רגלים can pass in under a year. But it asks how a full year could ever pass without three רגלים passing too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: For both a בכור and all קדשים, once a year has passed without the רגלים, or the רגלים have passed without a year, the owner breaks בל תאחר. It makes sense that the רגלים can pass without a year. But a year without the רגלים, how can that happen?
steps.whatsHappening: Using the word גופא, the גמרא returns to examine the בריתא on its own terms. It asks how the first case in the בריתא, a year without three רגלים, could ever happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three רגלים can easily pass in about half a year, for example from פסח through סוכות. But every year contains all three רגלים, so it seems impossible for a full year to go by without three רגלים passing. The גמרא wants to know what real case the בריתא has in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: we go back to study a source that was quoted earlier
Firstborn animal, which must be given to a כהן and offered
Consecrated offerings
The three pilgrimage festivals: פסח, שבועות, סוכות
It makes sense / granted (introduces the easy part before the hard part)
You can find it, meaning there is a real case where this happens

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not challenging רבא anymore. That discussion is finished. Now it is asking a new, practical question about the בריתא itself.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Both a firstborn and all consecrated offerings,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָבְרוּ עֲלֵיהֶם שָׁנָה בְּלֹא רְגָלִים,
phrases.english: once a year has passed over them without the Festivals,
or the Festivals without a year,
he transgresses "You shall not delay."

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא רְגָלִים בְּלֹא שָׁנָה מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ,
phrases.english: Granted, Festivals without a year, you can find that case;
but a year without the Festivals,
how can you find that case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבא discussion and goes back to the בריתא from Step 6 to examine its cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real situation where a full year passes but three רגלים have not.

steps.title: Sharpening the question: the case works only if Festivals must be in order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the question. For the view that the רגלים must pass in order (כסדרן), a year without three רגלים is easy to find. The real difficulty is for the view that does not require order.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who holds the רגלים must be in order: you can find the case. But for the one who does not hold they must be in order, how can you find it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens its question. It explains which opinion has no problem and which opinion the question is really aimed at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רגלים must start with פסח, then a person who vows just before שבועות waits until סוכות of the following year. A full year passes long before that, so the case is easy. If any three רגלים count in any order, then any three in a row are enough, and they always pass within one ordinary year. So for that view a case is still needed. Steps 12–16 supply it.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one view; introduces a problem for the other)
According to the one who holds
In their order: the רגלים must pass starting from פסח

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who holds they must be in order;
you can find the case.
But according to the one who does not hold they must be in order,
how can you find the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question of Step 10 so that it is aimed only at the view that does not require כסדרן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a year without three רגלים is possible for the view that the רגלים need not be in order.

steps.title: For רבי, it happens in a leap year, since he counts a solar year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer. According to רבי, the case happens in a שנה מעוברת, because רבי holds that a 'full year' means 365 days, the length of a solar year. The discussion continues next.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to רבי: you can find it in a leap year. As it was taught about "a full year": רבי says, one counts 365 days, like the number of days in the solar year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a partial answer that works for רבי's view, and backs it up with a בריתא about the 'full year' of houses in walled cities. The word בשלמא signals that the גמרא is setting up a question about the other view (the רבנן) next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leap year has 13 lunar months, about 384 days. רבי says a 'year' is only 365 days. So in a leap year, 365 days can run out before the same festival comes around again, and before the third רגל arrives. Step 14 builds the exact case.

keyTerms.meaning: Leap year: a year with an extra month added
A full year: the phrase from the פסוק about selling a house in a walled city
Days of the sun: the solar year of 365 days

steps.confusionAlert: The בריתא of 'שנה תמימה' is really about houses in walled cities, not about קדשים. The גמרא borrows רבי's definition of 'a year' from there.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi, you can find it
in a leap year.
As it is taught: "A full year":
phrases.notes: ויקרא כה:ל, about redeeming a house in a walled city.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹנֶה שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת וְשִׁשִּׁים וַחֲמִשָּׁה יוֹם
phrases.english: One counts three hundred sixty-five days,
like the number of days of the solar year,

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ בְּשָׁנָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to Step 11's question, but only for רבי's view. This sets up a question about the רבנן's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי, a year is 365 days. In a leap year, that can end before three רגלים have passed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בריתא about 'שנה תמימה' for houses in walled cities, where רבי defines a year as 365 days.

steps.title: The Rabbis' view of a full year in the walled-city בריתא
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא continues. The חכמים say a year is counted as twelve months from date to date, and in a leap year the extra month is added in the seller's favor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: He counts twelve months from day to day. And if the year was made a leap year, it is made a leap year for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the בריתא it started in the last step. Now we hear the חכמים, who disagree with רבי about what a 'full year' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said a full year is 365 days. The חכמים say a year runs from a date to the same date twelve months later. In a שנה מעוברת the year becomes thirteen months, because the extra month counts too. This matters because a 13-month year will always contain all three רגלים, so a leap year cannot solve the question for the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, here disagreeing with רבי
From a date to the same date (a full calendar span)
The year was made a leap year (an extra month of אדר was added)

steps.confusionAlert: 'נתעברה לו' means the extra month is added to his time. It does not mean the leap month is ignored. For the חכמים, a leap year is a full 13 months.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹנֶה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם,
phrases.english: He counts twelve months from day to day,
phrases.notes: From the date of sale to the same date the next year

phrases.english: and if the year was made a leap year, it is a leap year for him.
phrases.notes: The seller gets thirteen months to buy back the house

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: מוֹנֶה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בריתא whose first half (רבי's view) was quoted in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים define a year as twelve months from date to date, with a leap month counted as part of the year.

steps.title: The case according to רבי: consecrated after פסח in a leap year
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי, a person consecrates an animal after פסח in a leap year. By the end of אדר שני, 365 days have passed, but פסח has not come around again.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can find this case according to רבי: where he consecrated it after the festival of פסח. When he reaches the end of the second אדר, the year is full, but the רגלים are not yet complete.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses רבי's definition (365 days) to build an actual case. In it, a full year passes without all three רגלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone consecrates after פסח, so the next two רגלים to pass are שבועות and סוכות. In a שנה מעוברת there is an extra אדר, so by the end of אדר שני about 365 days have gone by. That is a full year for רבי, yet the third רגל, פסח, has not arrived yet.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find it (this is a possible case)
He consecrated it (made the animal הקדש)
The end of
The second אדר (the added month in a leap year)

phrases.english: You can find it according to רבי
where he consecrated it after the festival of Matzos (פסח),
so that when he reaches the end of the second Adar,
the year is full, but the Festivals are not complete.
phrases.notes: 365 days have passed, but פסח has not come yet

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ לְרַבִּי דְּאַקְדְּשַׁהּ בָּתַר חַג הַמַּצּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי's 365-day definition from the בריתא to build a concrete case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי: consecrated after פסח in a leap year, so 365 days end with אדר שני before פסח returns.

steps.title: How can the case happen according to the Rabbis?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a year without three רגלים is possible for the רבנן, who count a leap year as a full thirteen months.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the רבנן, how can you find this case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the leap-year answer only works for רבי. It now asks for a case that works for the רבנן, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, a leap year is thirteen months long, so it always includes all three רגלים. The leap-year trick does not help them. A different kind of case is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the same as the חכמים of the בריתא)
How?

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis, how can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having solved the question for רבי, the גמרא asks for the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scenario where twelve months from date to date pass without all three רגלים, according to the רבנן.

steps.title: רב שמעיה: שבועות can fall on the 5th, 6th, or 7th of סיון
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה taught that שבועות moves between the 5th, 6th, and 7th of סיון, depending on whether ניסן and אייר are full or short months. This produces a year without three רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב שמעיה taught: עצרת is sometimes on the fifth, sometimes on the sixth, and sometimes on the seventh. How so? If both are full, it falls on the fifth. If both are short, on the seventh. If one is full and one is short, on the sixth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question for the רבנן by quoting רב שמעיה. Because the date of שבועות can shift, a date-to-date year can end before שבועות arrives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבועות is the fiftieth day of the עומר count, not a fixed date, so its date depends on the lengths of ניסן and אייר. Suppose שבועות fell on 5 סיון and someone vowed on 6 סיון. If next year שבועות falls on 7 סיון, his twelve months end on 6 סיון, before שבועות. Only סוכות and פסח have passed.

keyTerms.meaning: שבועות
Full months (30 days)
Short months (29 days)
How so? (introducing an explanation)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Five, six, seven' refers to the date in סיון, not a number of days. Fuller months mean the fifty days end earlier in סיון, which is why two full months give the 5th.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that, according to רב שמעיה, the calendar months were set by actual sighting of the new moon, so their lengths could vary.

phrases.english: As Rav Shemaya taught:
Shavuos is sometimes on the fifth,
sometimes on the sixth, sometimes on the seventh.
How so?
If both are full, the fifth,
phrases.notes: Both ניסן and אייר have 30 days

phrases.english: if both are short, the seventh,
if one is full and one is short, the sixth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 using a teaching about the shifting date of שבועות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For the רבנן: vow on 6 סיון after שבועות fell on the 5th. Next year שבועות falls on the 7th, so the year ends before שבועות.

steps.title: Who disagrees with רב שמעיה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the opposite of רב שמעיה, namely that שבועות always falls on a fixed date.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who disagrees with רב שמעיה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a side comment. It asks who holds the opposite view, and sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שמעיה's teaching implies that month lengths vary. The גמרא wants to identify the תנא who believes the months follow a fixed pattern, so that the date of שבועות never changes.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period
Who disagrees with him

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמַעְיָה —
phrases.english: And who is the Tanna who disagrees with Rav Shemaya?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמַעְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question that follows from רב שמעיה's teaching.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that the months have fixed lengths.

steps.title: אחרים: the yearly gap is always four days (five in a leap year)
steps.stepSummary: The disagreeing view is אחרים, who say שבועות and ראש השנה each move only four weekdays from one year to the next, or five in a leap year. This implies a fixed calendar.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is אחרים. As it was taught: אחרים say: Between עצרת and עצרת, and between ראש השנה and ראש השנה, there are only four days. And if it was a leap year, five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אחרים disagree with רב שמעיה. It quotes a בריתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים hold that the months always alternate between 30 and 29 days, so a regular year is 354 days, which is fifty weeks plus four days. In their fixed scheme a leap year is 383 days, which is fifty-four weeks plus five days, matching the 'five' in the ברייתא. On a fixed schedule, ניסן and אייר are always one full and one short, so שבועות always lands on 6 סיון. That contradicts רב שמעיה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a name for a תנא (identified with רבי מאיר)
There is no difference between, except
A leap year

steps.confusionAlert: 'Four days' means the holiday shifts four days of the week (for example, from Sunday to Thursday). It does not mean the year is four days long.
steps.whatToRemember: רב שמעיה: month lengths vary, so שבועות can be on 5, 6, or 7 סיון. אחרים: months are fixed, so the holiday shifts a set number of weekdays each year.

phrases.english: It is Acherim.
As it was taught: Acherim say:
Between Shavuos and Shavuos,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: and between Rosh Hashanah and Rosh Hashanah,
there are only four days.
And if it was a leap year, five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by naming אחרים and quoting their בריתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחרים, who hold a fixed calendar in which the yearly gap is four weekdays (five in a leap year).

steps.title: רבי זירא: does an heir violate בל תאחר?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether a יורש who inherits his father's unpaid vow violates בל תאחר. One side says the verse speaks of the one who vowed. The other side says the verse speaks of the one obligated to bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: What about an heir regarding 'do not delay'? The Torah says 'When you vow a vow', and this one did not vow. Or perhaps it says 'And you shall come there and you shall bring there', and this one is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. רבי זירא asks whether the איסור of delaying a vow passes to an heir, and lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the פסוק of בל תאחר begins 'כי תדור נדר', so it applies only to the person who made the vow, and the heir never vowed. Side two: the פסוק 'ובאת שמה והבאתם שמה' (which is learned with בל תאחר) focuses on bringing, and the heir is obligated to bring his father's קרבן. So perhaps he too violates by delaying.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a genuine question of law)
An heir
The prohibition 'do not delay' paying a vow
Or perhaps
He is obligated

steps.whyThisMatters: The question asks whether בל תאחר is tied to the person who made the vow or to the obligation itself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
An heir, what is the law regarding 'do not delay'?
'When you vow a vow', the Merciful One said,
and this one did not vow,
or perhaps:
'And you shall come there, and you shall bring there',
and this one is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא: יוֹרֵשׁ, מַהוּ בְּ״בַל תְּאַחֵר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic within the laws of בל תאחר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an heir who must bring his father's vowed קרבן violates בל תאחר by delaying it.

steps.title: רבי חייא's ברייתא: an heir is excluded
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי חייא reads the word מֵעִמָּךְ as excluding an יורש from בל תאחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי חייא taught that the verse says 'from you', and this excludes an heir.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that answers רבי זירא's question from Step 19. An heir does not violate בל תאחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'ה׳ will demand it מֵעִמָּךְ, from you.' The word 'you' points to the person who made the vow. So the heir, who did not vow, is not included in the prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: From you (Devarim 23:22)
To exclude

steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the question about the heir: the verse is about the one who made the vow.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For Rabbi Chiyya taught:
"From you" — to exclude an heir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question about the heir.
steps.raayaObject: Whether an heir violates בל תאחר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's ברייתא on the word מֵעִמָּךְ

steps.title: The word is already used for gleanings, forgotten sheaves and the field's corner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that מֵעִמָּךְ is already needed to include לקט, שכחה and פאה in בל תאחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this word 'from you' is needed for something else: to include gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא. The same word was already used for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the word עִמָּךְ taught that delaying the gifts owed to the poor also violates בל תאחר. If the word is used up for that lesson, how can it also exclude an heir?

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (another lesson)
Gleanings left for the poor
Forgotten sheaves left for the poor
The corner of the field left for the poor

phrases.english: But this "from you" is needed for him
to teach gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the derivation in Step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One word cannot teach two lessons, and this word is already used for לקט, שכחה and פאה.

steps.title: Read the word two ways
steps.stepSummary: The verse is read both as עִמָּךְ and as מֵעִמָּךְ, so it yields two lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read it as 'with you' for one lesson, and read it as 'from you' for the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word teaches both lessons. Each lesson comes from a different reading of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עִמָּךְ, 'with you', includes the gifts to the poor. The extra letter מ makes it מֵעִמָּךְ, 'from you', and that extra letter excludes the heir.

keyTerms.meaning: Read into it (read the word another way)
With you

phrases.english: Read into it "with you",
and read into it "from you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Double reading of a single word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word can teach only one lesson.
steps.terutzMaskana: עִמָּךְ includes the poor's gifts, and the extra מ excludes the heir.
steps.whatToRemember: An heir does not violate בל תאחר. The extra מ in מֵעִמָּךְ excludes him.

steps.title: Does a woman violate the prohibition against delaying?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether a woman is subject to בל תאחר. She is not obligated in ראיה, but she is obligated in שמחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: what is the law for a woman regarding 'do not delay'? Do we say she is exempt, since she is not obligated to appear at the Temple? Or perhaps she is included, since she is obligated to rejoice on the festival?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא opens a new question about a woman who made a vow. He lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בל תאחר is tied to the passing of the רגלים. A woman is exempt from appearing at the Temple, which points to her being exempt. But she is obligated to rejoice on the festival, which may tie her to the רגלים enough to be included.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks (an open question)
The obligation to appear at the Temple on the festival
The obligation to rejoice on the festival
Or perhaps

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
A woman, what is her law regarding "do not delay"?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן: הָא לָא מִיחַיְּיבָא בִּרְאִיָּה,
phrases.english: Do we say: she is not obligated in appearing,
or perhaps: she is obligated in rejoicing?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא: אִשָּׁה, מַה הִיא בְּ״בַל תְּאַחֵר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question in the same topic of בל תאחר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a woman is subject to בל תאחר

steps.title: אביי: her obligation to rejoice decides it
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the answer follows from her obligation in שמחה, so she is subject to בל תאחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Just derive it from the fact that she is obligated in rejoicing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי זירא. Since a woman is obligated to rejoice on the festival, she does violate בל תאחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי treats the second side of the question as decisive. Her obligation in שמחה connects her to the festival, so delaying her vow past the festival violates the prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Just derive it from (it is obvious from)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Derive it from the fact that she is obligated in rejoicing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A woman is subject to בל תאחר because she is obligated in שמחה.

steps.title: Elsewhere אביי says her husband makes her rejoice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי from his own statement that a woman's husband makes her rejoice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did אביי really say this? But אביי himself said: a woman, her husband makes her rejoice!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two statements of אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband makes her rejoice, then the obligation of שמחה is on him, not on her. In that case she has no personal obligation in שמחה, and אביי's answer in Step 24 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say?
But didn't he say?
Her husband makes her rejoice

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying a woman has no festival joy. He is saying the obligation to provide it falls on her husband, not on her.

phrases.english: And did Abaye say this?
But didn't Abaye say:
A woman — her husband makes her rejoice!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר אַבָּיֵי הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that a woman is obligated in שמחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי elsewhere places the obligation of שמחה on the husband, not the woman.

steps.title: אביי was speaking according to רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: אביי's answer follows רבי זירא's own view that a woman is obligated in שמחה. It is not אביי's own opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was speaking according to the view of רבי זירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. אביי was answering inside רבי זירא's own way of thinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא holds that a woman herself is obligated in שמחה. So אביי told him that, by his own view, the question answers itself. אביי personally holds that the husband carries the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his (the other person's) view
He was saying

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי זירא, a woman is obligated in שמחה, so she is subject to בל תאחר. אביי's own view is that her husband makes her rejoice.

phrases.english: He was speaking according to the words of Rabbi Zeira.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Statement made according to another's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי personally holds that a woman is obligated in שמחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי answered according to רבי זירא's view. His own view places the obligation on the husband.

steps.title: When does the firstborn's year start?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a question: from what point is the one-year deadline for a בכור counted?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: for a firstborn animal, from when do we count its year?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. A בכור has a one-year deadline, and the question is when that year begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps discussed בל תאחר, the ban on delaying offerings. A בכור is given to the כהן and must be brought within its year. There are two possible starting points: the day it is born, or the day it first becomes fit to be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים)
A firstborn male kosher animal, which is holy and given to the כהן
From when?
We count

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
phrases.notes: Standard way to open a real question.

phrases.english: A firstborn animal: from when do we count its year?
phrases.notes: The year by which it must be brought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the woman's obligation in בל תאחר to a new question: when the time limit for a בכור begins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the בכור's year begin at birth, or when it becomes fit to be offered?

steps.title: אביי: the year starts at birth
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the בכור's year is counted from the moment it is born.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: we count from the time it is born.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his answer: the year starts the day the animal is born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the year starts with the animal's life itself. It does not matter that the animal cannot be offered during its first seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: From the time it was born

phrases.english: Abaye said:
From the time it is born.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The year is counted from birth.

steps.title: רב אחא: the year starts when the animal is fit to be offered
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב rules that the year is counted from the eighth day, when the animal can first be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: we count from the time it is fit to be accepted as an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer: the year starts only once the animal can be brought on the מזבח, which is its eighth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says a newborn animal cannot be offered until its eighth day (ויקרא כב:כז). רב אחא בר יעקב holds that the deadline cannot start before the animal is even fit to be offered. So he and אביי seem to disagree by seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: Being accepted as an offering, i.e. fit for the מזבח
Fit, suitable

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read שֶׁנִּרְאָה here as 'seen.' It means 'fit, suitable.' It is the eighth day, when the animal may first be offered.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
From the time it is fit to be accepted as an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an answer that appears to disagree with אביי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The year is counted from the eighth day, when the animal is fit to be offered.

steps.title: They do not really argue: one view is about an unblemished firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reconcile the two views. The view counting from fitness is about a בכור תם, an unblemished firstborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree. This one is about an unblemished firstborn...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to show that אביי and רב אחא בר יעקב are talking about different cases. This passage gives only the first case. The second half of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תם (unblemished) בכור must be offered on the מזבח, so its year starts only when it becomes fit, on the eighth day. That is רב אחא בר יעקב's view. The other case, which will explain אביי's view, is not yet stated here.

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not disagree
Unblemished, so fit for the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'הָא בְּתָם' goes with רב אחא בר יעקב, who counts from the eighth day. It does not go with אביי.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
This one is about an unblemished animal,
phrases.notes: רב אחא's view; the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent disagreement between steps 28 and 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each view refers to a different kind of בכור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי and רב אחא בר יעקב truly disagree about every בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: For an unblemished בכור, the year starts when it is fit to be offered. The other case, which explains אביי's view, follows on the next amud.
